A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Questioner–Solver code-translation work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning and translation experiments, including success rates, CodeBLEU scores and debug-round analyses in Tables 2–5 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds a test-coverage audit, model-configuration experiments and feedback ablations in Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The proposed Questioner–Solver pipeline, verification stages, seven-iteration rejection threshold and dialogue/QS-Pair construction remain unchanged. NoExec is an experimental control, not a replacement for the proposed method. Prompt changes are descriptive headings and minor copy edits.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Fortran-to-C++, C++-to-CUDA, the CodeParrot and CodeRosetta sources, HPC-Fortran-Cpp and the same principal evaluation sets. The new model study uses a sampled subset; no additional language, domain or distinct task scenario is documented.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark baselines remain unchanged. New Tables 8–9 add NoExec as an explicit comparison control alongside existing settings, while Table 7 adds a supplementary comparison of DeepSeek and Llama generator configurations.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluation design with gcov line/branch coverage, a model-and-temperature sweep on 100 sampled tasks with one 64-sample exception, and controlled removal of execution feedback. The original benchmark splits, fine-tuning hyperparameters and inference temperature remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct investigation of generated-test coverage, robustness across generator models and temperatures, feedback-message distributions, and NoExec ablations on both translation tasks. These address test quality, backbone sensitivity and the contribution of execution feedback, which v1 did not directly analyze.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. V2's additional sample counts, temperatures and runtime measurements do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New findings include 87.3% line coverage, 83.8% branch coverage, model success/runtime results and feedback distributions. Tables 8–9 newly report NoExec unit-test success of 73.93% for Fortran2CPP and 65.72% for CPP2CUDA. Tables 2–4 retain their original values; Table 5 changes only rounding.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same translation mapping and dialogue/QS-Pair definitions. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction's closing claim shifts from establishing a general paradigm across low-resource and domain-specific settings to improvements across multiple open-weight model families. The central pipeline, dataset, supervision-format and small-model competitiveness contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the small NoExec differences as evidence favoring structural/syntactic supervision over explicit execution feedback. Appendices A–B add backbone-robustness arguments and error-recovery explanations. The limitations emphasize missing performance feedback but remove earlier caveats about simplified environments and dependence on base-model reasoning.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-data repository pointer and discloses approximately 4–6 GPU hours per fine-tuning experiment. Table 7 documents additional temperatures, quantization identifiers, runtimes and failed runs. Table 6 corrects Llama 4 Scout's open-weight status from No to Yes; existing training details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds or substitutes citations including OMPGPT, Data Race Detection Using Large Language Models, ParEval-Repo and AutoParLLM, and replaces the Gemini 1.5 reference with Gemini 2.5. Some earlier references disappear, but the central positioning around dialogue-based translation supervision remains.

P1.justification: V2 edits grammar and affiliations, rearranges experiment subsection headings, condenses parts of the results discussion, rewrites the conclusion and replaces generic prompt headings with descriptive titles. Most existing method prose and prompt bodies are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 7–9, revises the architecture and pipeline diagrams, moves Figure 1 onto the first page, and exchanges the numbering and placement of the debug-round figures. Table 4 gains a size column, while Table 5 is reformatted with shorter numerical precision.

improvement.justification: The coverage audit, NoExec ablation and reporting of alternative-model failures add useful validation absent in v1; the repository pointer and training-time disclosure improve transparency. The net gain is limited: Table 7 omits the iteration statistics promised by its discussion, and the revised limitations remove useful caveats about simplified environments and base-model dependence.
